phases.label: Cluster admin
phases.blurb: Helm, Kustomize, CRDs, kubeadm, static Pods, etcd

phases.label: Failure drills
phases.blurb: Image, probe, DNS, CoreDNS, node & control-plane incidents

labModes.api: API lab: multi-node kind/minikube cluster with kubectl, Metrics Server, an Ingress controller, a default StorageClass, and a Gateway API implementation.
labModes.vm: VM lab: Ubuntu 22.04 kubeadm VMs with SSH and sudo, using the static-Pod model and etcd on the control plane.

tasks.title: Fix context and namespace
tasks.context: Current context is wrong.
tasks.objective: Switch to context cka-admin and set its default namespace to team-a.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.contexts[0].name}{" "}{.contexts[0].context.namespace}'
tasks.learningOutcomes: Context hygiene; namespace safety; exam discipline.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace team-a --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
CUR=$(kubectl config current-context)
kubectl config rename-context "$CUR" cka-admin 2>/dev/null || true
CLUSTER=$(kubectl config view -o jsonpath='{.contexts[?(@.name=="cka-admin")].context.cluster}')
USER=$(kubectl config view -o jsonpath='{.contexts[?(@.name=="cka-admin")].context.user}')
kubectl config set-context decoy --cluster="$CLUSTER" --user="$USER" --namespace=default >/dev/null
kubectl config use-context decoy
tasks.solution:
kubectl config use-context cka-admin
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=team-a

tasks.title: Least-privilege ServiceAccount
tasks.context: Namespace team-a needs a scoped identity.
tasks.objective: Create ServiceAccount app-reader with permission to get/list/watch Pods only.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:team-a:app-reader -n team-a && echo ; kubectl auth can-i create deployments --as=system:serviceaccount:team-a:app-reader -n team-a
tasks.learningOutcomes: RBAC primitives; least privilege; subject testing.
tasks.setup: kubectl create namespace team-a --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
tasks.solution:
kubectl -n team-a create serviceaccount app-reader
kubectl -n team-a create role pod-reader --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods
kubectl -n team-a create rolebinding app-reader-binding --role=pod-reader --serviceaccount=team-a:app-reader

tasks.title: Enforce restricted Pod Security
tasks.context: Namespace prod must apply Pod Security Admission.
tasks.objective: Label namespace prod so the restricted policy is enforced, warned, and audited.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl get ns prod -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.pod-security\.kubernetes\.io/enforce}{" "}{.metadata.labels.pod-security\.kubernetes\.io/warn}{" "}{.metadata.labels.pod-security\.kubernetes\.io/audit}'
tasks.learningOutcomes: Pod admission; PSA labels; namespace policy.
tasks.setup: kubectl create namespace prod --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
tasks.solution: kubectl label ns prod pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn=restricted pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit=restricted --overwrite

tasks.title: Install a local Helm chart
tasks.context: A local chart is staged at /opt/cka/charts/nodeecho.
tasks.objective: Install local chart /opt/cka/charts/nodeecho as release nodeecho in namespace ops.
tasks.verifyCmd: helm status nodeecho -n ops -o json | grep -q '"status":"deployed"' && echo OK
tasks.learningOutcomes: Helm release workflow; chart install; namespace targeting.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace ops --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
helm uninstall nodeecho -n ops 2>/dev/null || true
tasks.solution: helm install nodeecho /opt/cka/charts/nodeecho -n ops --create-namespace

tasks.title: Apply a Kustomize overlay
tasks.context: A Kustomize base + overlays live under /opt/cka/kustomize/web.
tasks.objective: Apply overlays/prod so Deployment web in web-prod runs 3 replicas of registry.k8s.io/nginx:1.29.
hints: inspect overlay diff first if desired
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n web-prod get deploy web -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}{" "}{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace web-prod --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n web-prod delete deploy web 2>/dev/null || true
tasks.solution: kubectl apply -k /opt/cka/kustomize/web/overlays/prod

tasks.title: Register a CRD
tasks.context: A CRD skeleton is at /opt/cka/crd/widget-crd.yaml.
tasks.objective: Create CRD widgets.demo.sh from the skeleton.
hints: CRD name must be plural + group
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl get crd widgets.demo.sh -o jsonpath='{.spec.names.kind}{" "}{.spec.group}'
tasks.setup: kubectl delete crd widgets.demo.sh 2>/dev/null || true
tasks.solution:
kubectl apply -f /opt/cka/crd/widget-crd.yaml
kubectl get crd widgets.demo.sh

tasks.title: Install and configure an operator
tasks.context: An operator bundle is at /opt/cka/operator/widget-operator.yaml.
tasks.objective: Apply the bundle, then create a Widget named cache-sample in namespace operator-lab.
hints: Install the operator bundle first, then create the CR
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n operators get deploy widget-operator-controller-manager -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}{" "}{.metadata.name}' ; echo ; kubectl -n operator-lab get widget cache-sample -o name
tasks.setup: kubectl create namespace operator-lab --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
tasks.solution:
kubectl apply -f /opt/cka/operator/widget-operator.yaml
kubectl -n operators rollout status deploy/widget-operator-controller-manager
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: demo.sh/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: cache-sample
  namespace: operator-lab
spec:
  size: 1
EOF

tasks.title: Generate a kubeadm join command
tasks.context: On control-plane cp1 a new worker must join.
tasks.objective: Create a fresh worker join command and save it to /opt/answers/join-wk2.sh.
tasks.verifyCmd: grep -E '^kubeadm join ' /opt/answers/join-wk2.sh | wc -l
tasks.setup:
sudo mkdir -p /opt/answers
sudo rm -f /opt/answers/join-wk2.sh
tasks.solution:
sudo mkdir -p /opt/answers
kubeadm token create --print-join-command | sudo tee /opt/answers/join-wk2.sh

tasks.title: Author an HA kubeadm config
tasks.context: An HA control plane fronted by a load balancer is planned.
tasks.objective: Write /opt/answers/ha-cluster.yaml for a stacked-HA kubeadm cluster using lb.lab.local:6443 as controlPlaneEndpoint.
tasks.verifyCmd: grep -E 'controlPlaneEndpoint: "?lb\.lab\.local:6443"?' /opt/answers/ha-cluster.yaml | wc -l
tasks.learningOutcomes: HA control-plane design; kubeadm config authoring.
tasks.setup:
sudo mkdir -p /opt/answers
sudo rm -f /opt/answers/ha-cluster.yaml
tasks.solution:
sudo mkdir -p /opt/answers
cat <<'EOF' | sudo tee /opt/answers/ha-cluster.yaml
apiVersion: kubeadm.k8s.io/v1beta4
kind: ClusterConfiguration
kubernetesVersion: v1.35.2
controlPlaneEndpoint: "lb.lab.local:6443"
networking:
  podSubnet: 10.244.0.0/16
EOF

tasks.title: Upgrade a kubeadm node
tasks.context: Target version v1.35.2 packages are preloaded on cp1.
tasks.objective: Upgrade node cp1 to v1.35.2, completing any needed drain/uncordon steps.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl get node cp1 -o jsonpath='{.status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion}{" "}{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status}'
tasks.setup: echo 'VM lab: ensure cp1 is one minor below target and target packages are staged.'
tasks.solution:
sudo kubeadm upgrade plan
sudo kubeadm upgrade apply v1.35.2 -y
kubectl drain cp1 --ignore-daemonsets
sudo apt-mark unhold kubelet kubectl && sudo apt-get install -y kubelet=1.35.2-* kubectl=1.35.2-* && sudo apt-mark hold kubelet kubectl
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart kubelet
kubectl uncordon cp1

tasks.title: Create a static Pod
tasks.context: Kubelet on cp1 watches /etc/kubernetes/manifests.
tasks.objective: Create static Pod manifest /etc/kubernetes/manifests/mirror-nginx.yaml so a mirror Pod appears in kube-system.
hints: mirror Pods are suffixed with the node name
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n kube-system get pods | grep -c '^mirror-nginx-'
tasks.setup: sudo rm -f /etc/kubernetes/manifests/mirror-nginx.yaml
tasks.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | sudo tee /etc/kubernetes/manifests/mirror-nginx.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: mirror-nginx
  namespace: kube-system
spec:
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: registry.k8s.io/nginx:1.29
EOF

tasks.title: Take an etcd snapshot
tasks.context: etcd runs as a static Pod on the control plane.
tasks.objective: Save an etcd snapshot to /opt/backup/cka.db.
hints: certs come from the kubeadm PKI under /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd
tasks.verifyCmd: test -s /opt/backup/cka.db && echo OK
tasks.setup:
sudo mkdir -p /opt/backup
sudo rm -f /opt/backup/cka.db
tasks.solution:
sudo mkdir -p /opt/backup
sudo ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /opt/backup/cka.db \
  --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key

tasks.title: Restore etcd state
tasks.context: A snapshot is provided at /opt/cka/backups/etcd-snapshot.db.
tasks.objective: Restore from the snapshot so ConfigMap restore-proof returns in kube-system.
hints: Restore to a new data dir
point the etcd static Pod manifest at the restored data dir
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n kube-system get cm restore-proof -o name
tasks.learningOutcomes: Disaster recovery; etcd restore; control-plane recovery.
tasks.setup: echo 'VM lab: snapshot containing configmap/restore-proof staged at /opt/cka/backups/etcd-snapshot.db.'
tasks.solution:
sudo ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot restore /opt/cka/backups/etcd-snapshot.db --data-dir /var/lib/etcd-restore
sudo sed -i 's#path: /var/lib/etcd#path: /var/lib/etcd-restore#' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml
sudo sed -i 's#--data-dir=/var/lib/etcd#--data-dir=/var/lib/etcd-restore#' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml
# kubelet recreates etcd from the restored data dir; wait for the API to settle
kubectl -n kube-system get cm restore-proof

tasks.title: Create a Deployment from dry-run YAML
tasks.context: Namespace ws-01 needs a basic web Deployment.
tasks.objective: Create Deployment web with 3 replicas using nginx:1.29, generated from imperative dry-run output and then applied.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n ws-01 get deploy web -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}{" "}{.spec.replicas}{" "}{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace ws-01 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n ws-01 delete deploy web 2>/dev/null || true
tasks.solution:
kubectl -n ws-01 create deployment web --image=nginx:1.29 --replicas=3 --dry-run=client -o yaml > web.yaml
kubectl apply -f web.yaml

tasks.title: Perform a rolling update
tasks.context: Deployment web in ws-02 runs nginx:1.29.
tasks.objective: Update it to nginx:1.30 and wait for rollout completion.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n ws-02 get deploy web -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}{" "}{.status.updatedReplicas}{" "}{.status.availableReplicas}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace ws-02 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n ws-02 create deployment web --image=nginx:1.29 --replicas=3 2>/dev/null || kubectl -n ws-02 set image deploy/web nginx=nginx:1.29
tasks.solution:
kubectl -n ws-02 set image deploy/web nginx=nginx:1.30
kubectl -n ws-02 rollout status deploy/web

tasks.title: Roll back a bad deployment
tasks.context: Deployment web in ws-03 was updated to a broken image.
tasks.objective: Roll it back to the previous stable revision (nginx:1.29).
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n ws-03 get deploy web -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}{" "}{.status.availableReplicas}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace ws-03 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n ws-03 create deployment web --image=nginx:1.29 --replicas=3 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n ws-03 rollout status deploy/web
kubectl -n ws-03 set image deploy/web nginx=nginx:does-not-exist
tasks.solution:
kubectl -n ws-03 rollout history deploy/web
kubectl -n ws-03 rollout undo deploy/web
kubectl -n ws-03 rollout status deploy/web

tasks.title: Inject a ConfigMap as a file
tasks.context: Deployment web in ws-04 should serve custom content.
tasks.objective: Make web serve hello-cm from /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html via a ConfigMap mount.
hints: Create the ConfigMap from a literal or file
mount the exact key path with subPath if needed
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n ws-04 exec deploy/web -- cat /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace ws-04 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n ws-04 create deployment web --image=nginx:1.29 2>/dev/null || true

tasks.title: Inject a Secret as an environment variable
tasks.context: Pod db-client in ws-05 needs a password from a Secret.
tasks.objective: Ensure db-client reads Secret key password as env var DB_PASSWORD with value s3cr3t!.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n ws-05 exec pod/db-client -- printenv DB_PASSWORD
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace ws-05 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n ws-05 delete pod db-client 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n ws-05 create secret generic db --from-literal=password='s3cr3t!' --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
tasks.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: db-client
  namespace: ws-05
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
    env:
    - name: DB_PASSWORD
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: db
          key: password
EOF

tasks.title: Fix scheduling with affinity and toleration
tasks.context: Pod batcher in ws-06 is Pending.
tasks.objective: Make it run on node wk2, which is labeled disk=ssd and tainted dedicated=batch:NoSchedule.
hints: Combine node affinity or nodeSelector with a matching toleration
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n ws-06 get pod batcher -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}{" "}{.status.phase}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace ws-06 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
WK2=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[?(@.spec.taints)].metadata.name}' | awk '{print $1}')
WK2=${WK2:-$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[1].metadata.name}')}
kubectl label node "$WK2" disk=ssd --overwrite
kubectl taint node "$WK2" dedicated=batch:NoSchedule --overwrite
kubectl -n ws-06 delete pod batcher 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n ws-06 run batcher --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600
tasks.solution:
kubectl -n ws-06 delete pod batcher --ignore-not-found
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: batcher
  namespace: ws-06
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    disk: ssd
  tolerations:
  - key: dedicated
    operator: Equal
    value: batch
    effect: NoSchedule
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

tasks.title: Configure an HPA
tasks.context: Deployment cpu-demo in ws-07 has CPU requests set.
tasks.objective: Create an HPA for cpu-demo with min 2, max 5, CPU target 60%.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n ws-07 get hpa cpu-demo -o jsonpath='{.spec.minReplicas}{" "}{.spec.maxReplicas}{" "}{.spec.metrics[0].resource.target.averageUtilization}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace ws-07 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n ws-07 delete hpa cpu-demo 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n ws-07 create deployment cpu-demo --image=registry.k8s.io/hpa-example 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n ws-07 set resources deploy/cpu-demo --requests=cpu=200m
tasks.solution: kubectl -n ws-07 autoscale deployment cpu-demo --min=2 --max=5 --cpu-percent=60

tasks.title: Build a basic StatefulSet
tasks.context: Namespace ws-08 needs stable identity + per-Pod storage.
tasks.objective: Create headless Service web-hl and StatefulSet web with 2 replicas and volumeClaimTemplates.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n ws-08 get svc web-hl -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}' ; echo ; kubectl -n ws-08 get pvc data-web-0 -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}'
tasks.learningOutcomes: Stateful identity; headless networking; per-Pod persistence.
tasks.setup: kubectl create namespace ws-08 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
tasks.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-hl
  namespace: ws-08
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: web
  ports:
  - port: 80
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: ws-08
spec:
  serviceName: web-hl
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.29
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: data
    spec:
      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 1Gi
EOF

tasks.title: Expose a Deployment as ClusterIP
tasks.context: Deployment api exists in sn-01.
tasks.objective: Expose api on Service port 8080 to container port 80 as ClusterIP.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n sn-01 get svc api -o jsonpath='{.spec.type}{" "}{.spec.ports[0].port}{" "}{.spec.ports[0].targetPort}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace sn-01 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n sn-01 create deployment api --image=nginx:1.29 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n sn-01 delete svc api 2>/dev/null || true
tasks.solution: kubectl -n sn-01 expose deployment api --name=api --port=8080 --target-port=80 --type=ClusterIP

tasks.title: Create a fixed NodePort Service
tasks.context: Deployment api exists in sn-02.
tasks.objective: Expose api as NodePort 30080 (Service named api-np).
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n sn-02 get svc api-np -o jsonpath='{.spec.type}{" "}{.spec.ports[0].nodePort}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace sn-02 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n sn-02 create deployment api --image=nginx:1.29 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n sn-02 delete svc api-np 2>/dev/null || true
tasks.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api-np
  namespace: sn-02
spec:
  type: NodePort
  selector:
    app: api
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80
    nodePort: 30080
EOF

tasks.title: Create a LoadBalancer Service object
tasks.context: sn-03 needs a LoadBalancer Service object (local lab may emulate the LB).
tasks.objective: Create Service api-lb of type LoadBalancer for port 80.
hints: Focus on a correct spec even if the local lab emulates the LB
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n sn-03 get svc api-lb -o jsonpath='{.spec.type}{" "}{.spec.ports[0].port}'
tasks.learningOutcomes: Service API fluency; exam object creation.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace sn-03 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n sn-03 create deployment api --image=nginx:1.29 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n sn-03 delete svc api-lb 2>/dev/null || true
tasks.solution: kubectl -n sn-03 expose deployment api --name=api-lb --port=80 --target-port=80 --type=LoadBalancer

tasks.title: Repair a broken selector so backends appear
tasks.context: Service web in sn-04 has no traffic because its selector is wrong.
tasks.objective: Fix it so the Service has 2 ready backends.
hints: Compare Service selector vs Pod labels
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n sn-04 get endpointslice -l kubernetes.io/service-name=web -o jsonpath='{.items[0].endpoints[*].conditions.ready}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace sn-04 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n sn-04 create deployment web --image=nginx:1.29 --replicas=2 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n sn-04 delete svc web 2>/dev/null || true
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: sn-04
spec:
  selector:
    app: wrong
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80
EOF
tasks.solution:
kubectl -n sn-04 patch svc web -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"web"}}}'
kubectl -n sn-04 get endpointslice -l kubernetes.io/service-name=web

tasks.title: Create a headless Service
tasks.context: Stateful Pods in sn-05 need stable per-Pod DNS.
tasks.objective: Create headless Service db-hl for the provided stateful Pods.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n sn-05 get svc db-hl -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace sn-05 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n sn-05 run db-0 --image=nginx:1.29 --labels=app=db 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n sn-05 delete svc db-hl 2>/dev/null || true
tasks.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: db-hl
  namespace: sn-05
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: db
  ports:
  - port: 80
EOF

tasks.title: Prove cross-namespace DNS works
tasks.context: Pod dns-client in namespace front must reach service api in namespace back.
tasks.objective: Make sure api.back resolves via cluster DNS from dns-client.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n front exec dns-client -- sh -c 'nslookup api.back.svc.cluster.local >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace front --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl create namespace back --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n back create deployment api --image=nginx:1.29 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n back expose deployment api --port=80 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n front delete pod dns-client 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n front run dns-client --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600
tasks.solution:
# The Service already exists; verify resolution from the client Pod.
kubectl -n front exec dns-client -- nslookup api.back.svc.cluster.local

tasks.title: Create default-deny ingress policy
tasks.context: Pods labeled app=api in sn-07 must be isolated.
tasks.objective: Deny ingress to Pods labeled app=api by default.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n sn-07 exec tester -- sh -c 'wget -qO- --timeout=2 http://api >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace sn-07 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n sn-07 create deployment api --image=nginx:1.29 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n sn-07 label deploy api app=api --overwrite
kubectl -n sn-07 expose deployment api --port=80 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n sn-07 delete pod tester 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n sn-07 run tester --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600
tasks.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-api
  namespace: sn-07
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api
  policyTypes: ["Ingress"]
  ingress: []
EOF

tasks.title: Allow only one namespace through policy
tasks.context: api in sn-08 should accept traffic only from namespace frontend.
tasks.objective: Permit traffic to api only from namespace frontend, while other stays blocked.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n frontend exec client -- sh -c 'wget -qO- --timeout=2 http://api.sn-08 >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?' ; echo ; kubectl -n other exec client -- sh -c 'wget -qO- --timeout=2 http://api.sn-08 >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?'
tasks.setup:
for ns in sn-08 frontend other; do kubectl create namespace $ns --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -; done
kubectl -n sn-08 create deployment api --image=nginx:1.29 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n sn-08 expose deployment api --port=80 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n frontend run client --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n other run client --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600 2>/dev/null || true
tasks.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-frontend
  namespace: sn-08
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Ingress"]
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: frontend
EOF

tasks.title: Configure path-based Ingress routing
tasks.context: sn-09 has blue-svc and green-svc backends and an Ingress controller installed.
tasks.objective: Create Ingress app routing /blue to blue-svc and /green to green-svc.
hints: Ensure the Ingress controller is present
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n sn-09 get ingress app -o jsonpath='{.spec.rules[0].http.paths[0].path}{" "}{.spec.rules[0].http.paths[1].path}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace sn-09 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
for c in blue green; do kubectl -n sn-09 create deployment $c --image=nginx:1.29 2>/dev/null || true; kubectl -n sn-09 expose deployment $c --name=$c-svc --port=80 2>/dev/null || true; done
tasks.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: sn-09
spec:
  rules:
  - http:
      paths:
      - path: /blue
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: blue-svc
            port:
              number: 80
      - path: /green
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: green-svc
            port:
              number: 80
EOF

tasks.title: Configure a simple Gateway API route
tasks.context: sn-10 has the Gateway API CRDs and a controller installed.
tasks.objective: Create a Gateway + HTTPRoute so route web is Accepted by the installed Gateway controller.
hints: Gateway API needs both the CRDs and an implementation
match gatewayClassName to the installed controller
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n sn-10 get httproute web -o jsonpath='{.status.parents[0].conditions[?(@.type=="Accepted")].status}{" "}{.status.parents[0].conditions[?(@.type=="ResolvedRefs")].status}'
tasks.learningOutcomes: Gateway API basics; modern ingress routing.
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace sn-10 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n sn-10 create deployment web --image=nginx:1.29 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n sn-10 expose deployment web --name=web-svc --port=80 2>/dev/null || true
tasks.solution:
GC=$(kubectl get gatewayclass -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: web-gw
  namespace: sn-10
spec:
  gatewayClassName: ${GC}
  listeners:
  - name: http
    protocol: HTTP
    port: 80
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: sn-10
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - name: web-gw
  rules:
  - backendRefs:
    - name: web-svc
      port: 80
EOF

tasks.title: Create and bind a static PV/PVC pair
tasks.context: st-01 needs a manually provisioned volume.
tasks.objective: Create PV pv-logs and PVC logs-pvc so the claim binds to that exact volume.
hints: Match size, access mode, class, and volumeName if needed
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n st-01 get pvc logs-pvc -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}{" "}{.spec.volumeName}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace st-01 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl delete pv pv-logs 2>/dev/null || true
tasks.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: pv-logs
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Gi
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath:
    path: /tmp/pv-logs
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: logs-pvc
  namespace: st-01
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  storageClassName: manual
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
  volumeName: pv-logs
EOF

tasks.title: Change reclaim policy to Retain
tasks.context: PV pv-logs releases storage on delete.
tasks.objective: Change PV pv-logs so released storage is retained instead of deleted.
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl get pv pv-logs -o jsonpath='{.spec.persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl delete pv pv-logs 2>/dev/null || true
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: pv-logs
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Gi
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Delete
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath:
    path: /tmp/pv-logs
EOF
tasks.solution: kubectl patch pv pv-logs -p '{"spec":{"persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy":"Retain"}}'

tasks.title: Use dynamic provisioning

tasks.objective: Create PVC dyn-pvc using StorageClass standard, mount it into Pod writer, and keep the claim Bound.
hints: Use the class explicitly for determinism

tasks.title: Create a WaitForFirstConsumer StorageClass
tasks.context: Topology-aware binding is needed in st-04.
tasks.objective: Create StorageClass slow-wffc with WaitForFirstConsumer, then create PVC data and a Pod that makes it bind.
hints: Binding stays Pending until a consumer Pod exists
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl get sc slow-wffc -o jsonpath='{.volumeBindingMode}' ; echo ; kubectl -n st-04 get pvc data -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}'
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace st-04 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl delete sc slow-wffc 2>/dev/null || true
PROV=$(kubectl get sc -o jsonpath='{.items[?(@.metadata.annotations.storageclass\.kubernetes\.io/is-default-class=="true")].provisioner}')
echo "default provisioner: ${PROV:-rancher.io/local-path}"
tasks.solution:
PROV=$(kubectl get sc -o jsonpath='{.items[0].provisioner}')
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: slow-wffc
provisioner: ${PROV}
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data
  namespace: st-04
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  storageClassName: slow-wffc
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: consumer
  namespace: st-04
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: data
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: data
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: data
EOF

tasks.title: Add persistent storage to an app and prove persistence
tasks.context: Deployment web in st-05 must keep data across Pod restarts.
tasks.objective: Attach PVC site-pvc to Deployment web, write /usr/share/nginx/html/marker.txt, restart the Pod, and keep the file.
hints: Mount the same claim into the replacement Pod
delete the Pod to prove persistence
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n st-05 exec deploy/web -- cat /usr/share/nginx/html/marker.txt
tasks.setup:
kubectl create namespace st-05 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n st-05 create deployment web --image=nginx:1.29 2>/dev/null || true
tasks.solution:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: site-pvc
  namespace: st-05
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
EOF
kubectl -n st-05 patch deploy web --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/volumes","value":[{"name":"site","persistentVolumeClaim":{"claimName":"site-pvc"}}]},
  {"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/volumeMounts","value":[{"name":"site","mountPath":"/usr/share/nginx/html"}]}
]'
kubectl -n st-05 rollout status deploy/web
kubectl -n st-05 exec deploy/web -- sh -c 'echo persistent-ok > /usr/share/nginx/html/marker.txt'
kubectl -n st-05 delete pod -l app=web
kubectl -n st-05 rollout status deploy/web

tasks.title: Recover CoreDNS after a bad config change
tasks.context: CoreDNS in kube-system is broken after an invalid Corefile edit.

hints: Inspect CoreDNS logs and the coredns ConfigMap
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl -n kube-system get deploy coredns -o jsonpath='{.status.availableReplicas}'
tasks.solution:
kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/coredns | tail
# restore a valid Corefile
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap coredns --type=merge -p '{"data":{"Corefile":".:53 {
    errors
    health
    ready
    kubernetes cluster.local in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa {
      pods insecure
      fallthrough in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa
    }
    forward . /etc/resolv.conf
    cache 30
    loop
    reload
    loadbalance
}
"}}'
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deploy coredns
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deploy coredns

tasks.title: Repair a broken control-plane component
tasks.context: API health is degraded because a control-plane static Pod manifest on cp1 has a bad flag.
tasks.objective: Restore readiness.
hints: Use /etc/kubernetes/manifests, kubelet logs, and manifest diffing
tasks.verifyCmd: kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose' | grep -c 'readyz check passed'
tasks.setup: echo 'VM lab: introduce an invalid flag into /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml.'
tasks.solution:
# on cp1:
sudo cp /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml /tmp/apiserver.bak
sudoedit /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml   # remove the bad flag

# wait for the kubelet to recreate the static Pod, then:
kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose'
